conviction_note: The main finding comes from peers that reported today. GS equities were +72% YoY with EPS $17.01 against $13.65, and JPM equities were +49%. The Zacks/Smartkarma equities estimates for MS ($4.51-4.9B, +10-19% YoY) look stale, which points to an EPS beat of roughly 8% on a $3.08 bar. The findings sum to +1.6. The scaled number is smaller (+0.63 = (2*0.57-1)*4.5) for three reasons: MS fell 1.2% today while GS rose, so the market did not pay for the read-through; the last large beat in July closed only +0.39%; and the evidence is peer proxy, not a company number.
bar: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of about $3.08 (TIKR/Yahoo, 2026-09-27: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/morgan-stanley-lagged-peers-ubs-094447004.html) and $3.12 (Hudson Labs, 2026-09-28: https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/morgan-stanley-q3-2026-earnings-preview-ms-results-preview), which agree within 1.3%. The outliers are Zacks at $2.83 and revenue of $19.63B (https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/markets/stocks/MS-N/pressreleases/5411613/morgan-stanley-stock-ahead-of-q3-earnings-buy-hold-or-sell/) and Earnings Whispers at $3.01. Revenue estimates run from $19.63B to $20.7B, so the revenue bar is disputed. Prior year was $2.80, Q2 2026 was $3.46.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 1.1% of float. 17.2M shares and 3.14 days to cover at the 2026-07-15 FINRA settlement (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/ms/short-interest/, via the sweep row). Not crowded. Skew_25d is -3.09 vol points (upside paid), put/call OI 0.46, and the event-implied move is 3.83%. The stock is -8.93% over 20 days and -17.8% off its 52-week high after private-credit fund redemption caps (09-18), the Asia deal-list leak review (09-23), UBS merger chatter (09-24) and a Wells Fargo target cut (09-25). MS closed 187.70 today, -1.2%, on the day GS rose on its beat.

findings.finding: Peers that reported 2026-10-13 point to an MS equities quarter well above stale estimates. GS equities were $6.44B (+72% YoY), driving EPS of $17.01 against $13.65 consensus. JPM equities were $4.95B (+49% YoY, a Q3 record). The MS equities estimates are $4.51B (Zacks, +9.6% YoY on $4.12B) and $4.9B (Smartkarma). If MS matches even the JPM rate, equities come in near $6.1B, about $1B+ above the estimate, worth roughly $0.30-0.45 of EPS on a $3.08 bar. Management's own pre-flag that '3Q is no 2Q' for markets is already in the sub-Q2 consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 brought record equities of $6.3B (+69%) and EPS $3.46 against about $2.94. The stock rose more than 2% premarket and closed only +0.39% on 2026-07-15. The three prints before that, all beats, closed +4.52%, +5.78% and +4.71%. MS is 4/4 up on prints in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: The GS and JPM prints are public as of this morning, so the sector read is partly in the price. MS still did not reprice: it closed -1.2% at 187.70 while GS rose 1-3%. The published MS segment estimates (Zacks equities $4.51B, EPS $2.83 cut 4.7% in a week) were set before the peer prints. If the read-through were priced, MS would have moved with GS today and the equities estimates would sit near $6B. The call-side skew (-3.09) shows some appetite for upside, which is the part of this already priced.
findings.independence: JPM equities +49% to $4.95B (https://www.tikr.com/blog/jpmorgan-misses-q3-estimates-but-dimons-buyback-cut-is-the-bigger-story, 2026-10-13). The Zacks MS segment estimates come from a separate document (https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/markets/stocks/MS-N/pressreleases/5411613/morgan-stanley-stock-ahead-of-q3-earnings-buy-hold-or-sell/). Both are peer and estimate documents. There is no MS-company number for Q3 trading, so this is a proxy.

findings.finding: Peer FICC and investment-banking lines were soft, which lands roughly on MS's flat consensus. JPM FICC was -4% YoY and missed, GS FICC -1%, and JPM underwriting fees fell short. Dealogic global IB revenue was -6.6% YoY in Q3, and LSEG global M&A volume fell 41% QoQ. Against that, GS IB fees were +21% YoY, and MS ranked #2 in YTD M&A advisory. MS consensus is FICC $2.16B (marginal decline) and IB $2.27B (flat), so the residual risk is a small miss on underwriting.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced MS reaction to an FICC or IB surprise in isolation. In the baseline's last four prints, equities and wealth dominated the narrative.
findings.source_date: 2026-10 (page undated in snippet; Q3 2026 LSEG data)
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The MS consensus already models flat IB and declining FICC, so this is filed small. If the market expected an IB miss, MS estimates would have been cut after BAC's 2026-09-14 guide of IB fees down more than 10%, and they were not.
findings.independence: JPM FICC miss (https://www.marketscreener.com/news/jpmorgan-s-3q-fixed-income-trading-revenue-misses-estimates-ce785dddd089f320, 2026-10-13). BAC IB guide (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/14/bank-of-america-bac-q3-investment-banking-fees.html, 2026-09-14). These are separate sources pointing the same way.

findings.finding: Wealth Management: fee-based asset-management fees are billed on beginning-of-period asset levels, and the S&P 500 rose about 15% in Q2 2026 and about 2% in Q3. The CFO guided Q3 NII to a modest sequential increase off Q2 wealth NII of $2.254B. The Fed then raised rates in September, which helps sweep yields but risks cash sorting. Net, this is a small positive that sits largely inside guidance.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 wealth record of $8.9B revenue, 30.5% margin and $148B NNA. That print still closed only +0.39%.
findings.why_not_priced: The NII guide is public and the market levels are public, so analysts model both. Only the Fed-hike increment came after the guide. If priced in full, it adds nothing. The Smartkarma estimate of $9.11B wealth revenue at a 30.8% margin suggests the bar already reflects this.
findings.independence: S&P 500 +2% in Q3 after +15% in Q2 (https://novelinvestor.com/2026-q3-returns/). Fed hike in September (https://fortune.com/2026/10/13/jpmorgan-goldman-sachs-citigroup-wells-fargo-interest-inflation/, 2026-10-13). Market-level proxy, not an MS number.

findings.finding: Co-president Simkowitz disclosed 'a couple of hundred million dollars of unrealized carry reversal, which is about $0.05 of EPS' tied to an infrastructure fund (quarter not named), a likely Investment Management headwind in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced MS reaction to a carry reversal. It is a below-segment-core item with no path to targets.
findings.why_not_priced: It was disclosed at a public conference, so analysts likely cut for it. The Zacks EPS cut of 4.7% in a week may partly reflect it. It is about 1.6% of EPS and one-off, so it is worth a fraction.
findings.independence: Same quote in TIKR's German version (https://www.tikr.com/de/blog/morgan-stanley-lagged-its-peers-after-ubs-merger-talk-and-a-target-cut-heres-what-the-stock-already-prices-in). It is the same document family, so it counts once.

findings.finding: The stock's 17.8% drawdown carries a named overhang: UBS merger speculation (Semafor, 2026-09-24, MS named only in analysis). Simkowitz framed capital use on 2026-09-15 as 'add on capabilities around our core business'. If the call is asked about M&A, a bolt-on answer would remove a discount, and a door-open answer would add to it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Per TIKR, MS fell -1.04% on 2026-09-24 on the Semafor report and lagged GS, JPM and C on the day. There is no earnings-day precedent.
findings.why_not_priced: The speculation is priced as a discount: forward P/E is about 15x against about 17x at end-June. What is not priced is management's answer on the call. If the market believed a large deal were off the table, the multiple gap to GS would have closed.
findings.independence: Yahoo/TIKR English version with the Simkowitz quote (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/morgan-stanley-lagged-peers-ubs-094447004.html). Same publisher, so it counts once.

Folded into finding 1 as the reason consensus sits below Q2. It sets the bar and is not a separate signal.

baseline_tension: The positive lean agrees with the call-side skew (-3.09, upside paid) and with MS's 4/4 up history. It cuts against the -8.9% 20-day run-up and against today's tape, where MS fell 1.2% on peer-beat day. That tape is why p_up sits at 57 and not above 60.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the July record-equities beat closed +0.39%, and MS fell on today's GS beat. Finding 1 cut from +2.0 to +1.5, and p_up from 59 to 57.
Rule 5 (proxy): the wealth fee/NII finding is a market-level proxy that sits largely inside the NII guide. Cut from +0.3 to +0.2.
Rule 2 (one-offs): the carry reversal is below-the-line Investment Management with no path to targets. Cut from -0.2 to -0.1.
Rule 6 (bar): $3.08 and $3.12 agree, so the bar is sourced by two estimates; no blanket cap. The Zacks $2.83 is flagged as an outlier.
'What has worked' (a peer print leaving consensus stale) supports keeping finding 1 as the main finding rather than cutting it further.
The FICC/IB finding and the M&A-overhang finding were left unchanged.
